html:
The capital of Chad, founded by the French as Fort-Lamy on 29 May 1900, at the meeting of the Chari and Logone rivers, after the Battle of Kousseri.

It was the seat of the French colony of Chad, part of French Equatorial Africa, and became the capital at independence in 1960. In 1973 Tombalbaye renamed it N'Djamena, from an Arabic phrase often translated as "place of rest". It was ruined in the fighting of 1979 and 1980, and rebels reached its gates in 2006 and 2008 before Idriss Deby's forces drove them back. It lies across the river from Cameroon.
